briefing.one_line: OpenAI raises funds, launches new API, while global regulators clamp down and AI compute capacity expands.

themes.title: OpenAI funding and new API
themes.text: OpenAI is negotiating a private funding round of up to $30 billion that would value the company at $1.25 trillion, led by Coatue and investors from the United Arab Emirates. The company also made its Decisions API generally available, offering voice and visual inputs at $0.10 per million input tokens.

stories.headline: OpenAI seeks up to $30 billion funding at $1.25 trillion valuation ahead of IPO
OpenAI launches Decisions API with voice, visual inputs at $0.10 per million tokens

themes.title: Governments tighten AI regulations
themes.text: Swedish government ministries have prohibited staff from using ChatGPT and Claude on work computers, requiring the use of Microsoft Copilot. India will issue a consultation paper on AI legislation in the coming weeks, and major U.S. banks are restricting third‑party AI agents from accessing customer accounts.

themes.title: OpenAI steps up safety
themes.text: OpenAI resumed training its most advanced models in an offline environment and added offline environments and high‑compute red‑teaming to improve containment. The company also terminated three safety researchers after an internal investigation alleged they leaked internal model designs.

themes.title: AI compute capacity expands
themes.text: SpaceX plans to expand its AI computing infrastructure to 13 GW by the end of 2027. Kazakhstan’s Firebird secured a U.S. export license for 45,000 NVIDIA Grace GPUs and is building a data center slated for commercial launch in Q3 2027.

weekly.title: DeepSeek's $15 B raise fuels AI funding war amid US bans
weekly.intro: The week saw a surge of capital into Chinese AI despite new U.S. restrictions, while safety concerns around autonomous agents intensified. At the same time, open‑weight models reshaped European AI strategy and enterprises across sectors accelerated AI adoption.
